description: This horizontal bar chart illustrates the difference in average Word Error Rate (WER) between two models—NESAC ft model (orange bars) and SESHA ft model (green bars)—when applied to various optimisations compared to a Whisper large baseline model. The vertical axis, labeled “Optimisations applied,” lists five categories in descending order of their WER difference: “Normalised,” “Add Spacing,” “Remove Spacing,” “Americanisms,” and “Dates.” The horizontal axis, labeled “Difference in Average WER from Whisper large,” uses a linear scale ranging from 0.000 to approximately 0.0035, with tick marks at intervals of 0.001. For each optimisation, two bars are shown side-by-side: the orange bar represents the NESAC ft model’s WER difference, and the green bar represents the SESHA ft model’s WER difference. The specific values are labeled at the end of each bar: for “Normalised,” the NESAC ft model has a difference of 0.00334 and the SESHA ft model has 0.00323; for “Add Spacing,” NESAC ft is 0.00319 and SESHA ft is 0.00344; for “Remove Spacing,” NESAC ft is 0.00311 and SESHA ft is 0.00306; for “Americanisms,” NESAC ft is 0.00299 and SESHA ft is 0.00302; and for “Dates,” NESAC ft is 0.00257 and SESHA ft is 0.00228. The bars are not sorted by value, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding and labeled values.
